summary:
MARS-X: Human Marswalk Mission Planner

MARS-X is an interactive 3D web app built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. It helps astronauts walk safely on Mars and get the most science from each trip.

The problem: Mars has no GPS. The ground is dangerous, with cliffs, soft sand dunes and loose rocks. Astronauts also have only 6–8 hours of oxygen and suit power per walk.

The solution: MARS-X plans the best walking route over real Mars terrain using one rule: safety first, then science, then efficiency. It compares three routes and picks the best one. In the Gale Crater test mission, Route B reached all 3 science targets with low risk and a science score of 94/100. The app maps 8 hazards by risk level, never allows slopes over 30°, and always blocks critical zones. If a dust storm, rockfall or loss of signal happens, it quickly works out a new safe path back to base.

Key features: 6 real Mars regions, a helmet view showing direction, slope and hazard warnings, live tracking of oxygen and suit power, and real NASA 3D models.

Built with: React, Three.js and NASA data (HiRISE, MOLA, CRISM, THEMIS, RAD).
details:
1. What does it do?

MARS-X is a browser-based, autonomous EVA mission planner and 3D simulator for future Mars astronauts. Because Mars lacks GPS, it guides surface navigation safely through:

  • Orbital Data Analysis: Combines four NASA PDS and USGS datasets (MOLA elevation, HiRISE 1m/px DTMs, CRISM minerals, and Curiosity REMS/RAD) to map terrain and hazards.
  • Autonomous Pathfinding: Uses a tuned A* algorithm to avoid radiation and slopes greater than 30°, generating three routes: Route A (fastest/oxygen-saving), Route B (balanced science vs. safety), and Route C (maximum hazard avoidance).
  • Orbit & Surface Views: Offers a 3D Martian globe with six high-resolution regions (Gale, Jezero, Olympus Mons, Valles Marineris, Hellas, Elysium) and a 1.75m first-person walk mode with WASD controls and an aerospace HUD (compass, pitch ladder, radar, suit telemetry).
  • Live Contingency Testing: Instantly recalculates safe return routes when Mission Control triggers dust storms, rockfalls, or comms failures.
  • Core Advantages: Provides GPS-free positioning, manages 6–8 hour oxygen/energy limits, targets high-value geological sites, reduces astronaut cognitive load, and runs at 60 FPS in any browser with zero installation.

2. What impact will this have?

  • Supports Artemis Moon-to-Mars: Equips 2030s Mars crews with autonomous surface navigation to boost survival and mission success.
  • Makes Data Actionable: Turns petabytes of raw orbiter data into usable, real-time navigation intelligence.
  • Open-Source Education: Gives students, researchers, and the public free access to explore real Martian terrain and simulate Marswalks.

3. What tools, technologies, and languages did you use?

  • Core & UI: JavaScript, GLSL, HTML5, CSS3, React 19, Web Components, Modular Glassmorphism CSS, GSAP
  • 3D & Build: Three.js (r173), WebGL 2.0, ACES Filmic, EffectComposer, UnrealBloomPass, glTF/GLB, Google Draco, Self-hosted WASM, Vite 6, Node.js, Git/GitHub
  • NASA & USGS Data: MGS MOLA, MRO HiRISE & CTX, MRO CRISM, MSL Curiosity (REMS/RAD), Mars 2020 (Mastcam-Z, SuperCam), USGS Geologic Map (SIM 3292), and NASA 3D Resources (TDRS, HDU, ACES)

4. How creative is your project?

  • Orbit-to-Surface Zoom: Smoothly transitions from an orbital view with atmospheric scattering and TDRS satellites down to a first-person surface walk.
  • Custom Multi-Spectral Shaders: Uses WebGL shaders with Nyquist anti-aliasing to render sharp 25m/100m contour lines alongside USGS stratigraphy and CRISM mineral maps without white-out.
  • NASA Assets & Glassmorphic HUD: Combines official NASA 3D models (TDRS, habitat, spacesuit) with an aerospace HUD displaying live suit, biomedical, and navigation data.

5. What factors did you take into consideration?

  • Biomechanics & Slopes: Models the metabolic energy of walking in a pressurized suit under 0.38g gravity and blocks slopes over 30° to prevent falls.
  • Life Support & Environment: Factors in PLSS limits (oxygen, battery, water) and real Martian conditions (7.2 hPa pressure, -48°C to -22°C, 0.68 mSv/day radiation).
  • Geological Diversity: Covers 4 billion years of Martian history across six contrasting zones, from Noachian clay lakebeds to Amazonian graben and volcanic scarps.
  • Speed & Reliability: Uses local procedural terrain and Draco-compressed assets for sub-2-second load times and crash-free 60 FPS demos.
